1377.13: The saloks of Sheikh Farid Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The day on which the bride is to be wed, its appointed hour has been written beforehand; the angel (of death), of whom one had only heard with one's ears, comes and shows his face; the poor humble soul is drawn out (of the body), the bones made to crack. The appointed hours that are written cannot be put off; make the soul understand this. The soul is the bride, death the bridegroom: he will wed her and take her away. Having sent (the soul) away with its own hands, on whose neck will (the body) run to fall? Have you not heard with your ears of the Pul Sirat, finer than a hair? O Farid, while the calls are sounding, do not stand by and let yourself be robbed. ॥1॥
Farid's saloks are in Lahnda (western Punjabi). Among its words that recur in them: ku, kun to; sanda, sandi, keri of; maida mine, taida yours; vanjna to go; theena to become; han I.
Saaha: the day fixed for a wedding, when the bride leaves her parents' home and which cannot be put off; here the appointed hour of leaving the world.
Pul Sirat (purslaat): in Islamic belief, the bridge over hell which every soul must cross after death.
1377.14: O Farid, the dervish's way at (the Lord's) door is hard, and I walk in the manner of the world; I have tied up a bundle and lifted it: where shall I go and throw it down? ॥2॥
1378.1: Nothing is understood, nothing is seen: the world is a hidden fire. My Master did well (by me); otherwise I too would have burned (in it). ॥3॥
1378.2: O Farid, had I known the sesame seeds were so few, I would have filled my cupped hands with care; had I known my Husband was so young, I would have been less proud. ॥4॥
At weddings in western Punjab, the bride and groom filled their cupped hands with sesame seeds and poured them into each other's; here the seeds are the breaths of life.
1378.3: Had I known the hem (I hold) would wear away, I would have tied a firm knot; (O Master,) there is none as great as you for me: I have wandered and seen the whole world. ॥5॥
1378.4: O Farid, if you are of subtle understanding, do not write black records (of others); bow your head and look within your own collar. ॥6॥
1378.5: O Farid, those who strike you with their fists, do not turn round and strike them; having kissed their feet, let us go to our own home. ॥7॥
1378.6: O Farid, when it was your time to earn, you were steeped in the world; the foundation of death grew firm, and when (the measure of life) was full, you had to depart. ॥8॥
1378.7: See, O Farid, what has come about: the beard has turned grey; what lies ahead has come near, and what lies behind is left far away. ॥9॥
1378.8: See, O Farid, what has come about: sugar has turned to poison; to whom but one's own Master can one tell this pain? ॥10॥
1378.9: O Farid, the eyes have grown weak with seeing, and the ears deaf with hearing; the branch (of the body) has come to ripeness and is taking on another colour. ॥11॥
1378.10: O Farid, those who did not enjoy (the Husband) while their hair was black, hardly one of them enjoys him when it is grey; love the Master, and the love will stay ever new. ॥12॥
1378.11: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O Farid, in black hair or grey, the Master is ever (present), if one keeps him in mind; (but) love does not take hold by one's own effort, though everyone may long for it; this cup of love is the Master's: he gives it to whomever he pleases. ॥13॥
1378.12: O Farid, the eyes that enchanted the world, those eyes I have seen: (once) they could not bear a line of kohl; they became a nest for the young of birds. ॥14॥
1378.13: O Farid, though one cries out and shouts and gives counsel day after day, those whom Satan has led astray, how can they turn their minds (back)? ॥15॥
1378.14: O Farid, become (like) the grass on the path, if you seek the Master in all; (when) one tears you and others trample you, then you will be admitted at the Master's door. ॥16॥
1378.15: O Farid, one should not speak ill of the dust; there is nothing as great as the dust: while we live it is under our feet, and when we die it is over us. ॥17॥
1378.16: O Farid, where there is greed, what love can there be? With greed, love is false. How long can the time be spent beneath a broken thatch when it rains? ॥18॥
1378.17: O Farid, why do you wander from forest to forest, trampling the thorns of the woods? God dwells in the heart: why do you search the forest? ॥19॥
1378.18: O Farid, on these little legs I roamed deserts and mountains; today, for me, Farid, the little water-pot (close by) has become a hundred kos away. ॥20॥
A kos is an old measure of distance, about two miles.
1378.19: O Farid, the nights are long, and the sides ache and smoulder; cursed is the life of those who rest their hope on others. ॥21॥
1379.1: O Farid, if I ever hold back (anything) from friends who come to me, my body burns like madder upon live coals. ॥22॥
1379.2: O Farid, the farmer wants the grapes of Bijaur, (yet) sows acacias; he goes about having wool spun, and wants to wear silk. ॥23॥
1379.3: O Farid, the lane is muddy, the house is far, and I love the Beloved: if I go, my blanket is soaked; if I stay, the love breaks. ॥24॥
1379.4: Let the blanket be soaked through and through, let the rain pour, as Allah wills; I will go and meet those friends, and let the love not break. ॥25॥
1379.5: O Farid, I worry over my turban, lest it get soiled; the heedless soul does not know that the dust eats up the head too. ॥26॥
1379.6: O Farid, brown sugar, white sugar, sugar candy, molasses, honey and buffalo's milk: these things are all sweet, (yet), O God, they do not come up to you. ॥27॥
1379.7: O Farid, my bread is (dry) as wood, and my hunger is its relish; those who have eaten buttered bread will suffer many pains. ॥28॥
1379.8: Eat your plain dry bread and drink cool water; O Farid, seeing another's buttered bread, let no one make his heart yearn. ॥29॥
1379.9: Today I did not sleep with my Husband, and my body aches as if it would break; go and ask the forsaken soul-brides: how does your night pass? ॥30॥
1379.10: She finds no shelter in her in-laws' home, and no place in her parents' home; her Husband does not ask after her at all, (yet) the bride's name is happy soul-bride. ॥31॥
The parents' home (peeaa) is this world; the in-laws' home (saahuraa) is the world beyond, where the soul-bride goes to her Husband Lord.
1379.11: In her in-laws' home and in her parents' home (alike, the bride) belongs to the Husband; the Husband is beyond reach and fathomless; O Nanak, she is the happy soul-bride who pleases the carefree Lord. ॥32॥
This salok, signed Nanak, is Guru Nanak Dev Ji's; it is also in Maru ki Vaar (Ang 1088), with a few small differences of wording.
1379.12: Bathed, washed and adorned, she came and slept without a care; O Farid, she remained smeared with (the smell of) asafoetida, and the scent of musk was gone. ॥33॥
1379.13: I do not fear the going of youth, if the love of the Husband does not go; O Farid, many a youth, without (his) love, has withered and dried up. ॥34॥
1379.14: O Farid, anxiety is my little bed, pain is its weave, and in separation (the same pain) is my mattress and quilt; this is our life: see it, O True Master. ॥35॥
1379.15: Separation, separation, one cries; (yet) O pang of separation, you are the king. O Farid, the body in which the pang of separation does not arise, know that body to be a cremation ground. ॥36॥
1379.16: O Farid, these (things of the world) are shoots of poison, coated in sugar and set out; some died while still sowing them, and some went, leaving what they had sown to ruin. ॥37॥
1379.17: O Farid, four (watches of the day) you wasted roaming about, and four (of the night) you wasted in sleep; God will ask for the account: for what work did you come? ॥38॥
1379.18: O Farid, have you gone to a door, to a gateway, and seen the gong (gharial)? Blameless, it is beaten: what will become of us, who are to blame? ॥39॥
The gharial is a metal gong on which the hours (gharis) and the watches were struck.
1379.19: Hour after hour it is beaten, and at every watch it receives its punishment; like the gong is that body whose night passes in pain. ॥40॥
1380.1: Sheikh Farid has grown old; his body has started to shake; even were one to live a hundred years, the body will still become dust. ॥41॥
1380.2: O Farid, (say,) O Master, do not let me sit at the door of another; if you would keep me so, draw the life out of my body. ॥42॥
1380.3: With an axe on his shoulder and a pitcher on his head, the blacksmith is master over the forest; O Farid, I seek my Husband, and you seek charcoal. ॥43॥
1380.4: O Farid, some have flour in plenty, and some have not even salt; when they have gone on ahead, they will be known (for what they are): (there it will be seen) who is to be beaten. ॥44॥
1380.5: (Those who had) kettle-drums beside them, a canopy over their heads, trumpets and songs of praise, have gone to sleep in the graveyard, and become one with the orphans. ॥45॥
1380.6: O Farid, those who built houses, pavilions and mansions have gone too; they made a false bargain, and came and lay down in graves. ॥46॥
1380.7: O Farid, the patched coat has many stitches, (but) the soul has not a single stitch; each in his turn, the great sheikhs and the sheikhs have gone. ॥47॥
1380.8: O Farid, while the two lamps (of the eyes) were burning, the angel (of death) came and sat down; he seized the fort (of the body), plundered the heart, and went, putting out the little lamps. ॥48॥
1380.9: O Farid, see what has befallen the cotton, what has befallen the sesame, the sugar-cane and the paper, the clay pot and the charcoal: such is the punishment of those who do evil deeds. ॥49॥
1380.10: O Farid, the prayer mat on the shoulder, the black woollen robe about the neck, a knife in the heart and molasses in the mouth: outside there seems to be light, and in the heart is the dark night. ॥50॥
1380.11: O Farid, not a drop of blood comes out, if one cuts open (their) body; the bodies that are dyed in God, in those bodies there is no blood. ॥51॥
1380.12: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). This body is all blood; without blood there is no body. Those who are dyed in their Husband: in that body is no blood of greed. When the fear (of God) enters, the body grows lean, and the blood of greed goes out of it. As metal is purified in fire, so the fear of the Lord removes the filth of an evil mind. O Nanak, beautiful are those people who, giving their love to the Lord, are dyed (in him). ॥52॥
1380.13: O Farid, search out that pool from which the real thing is found; what comes of searching a puddle? The hand only sinks in the mud. ॥53॥
1380.14: O Farid, when young, she did not enjoy her Husband, and grown old, she died; in the grave the bride cries out that she did not meet you, O Husband. ॥54॥
1380.15: O Farid, the head has turned white, the beard is white, and the moustache too is white; O heedless, crazy mind, why do you indulge in pleasures? ॥55॥
1380.16: O Farid, how far can one run on a rooftop? Cast off this sleep that keeps you from the Beloved; the numbered days you were given have gone, leaping away. ॥56॥
1380.17: O Farid, houses, pavilions and mansions: let no one fix his mind on these; when the unweighed earth falls (on you in the grave), none (of them) will be your friend. ॥57॥
1380.18: O Farid, do not set your heart on pavilions and wealth; keep mighty death in mind; remember that place to which you must go in the end. ॥58॥
1381.1: O Farid, the deeds that bring no good, give up those wretched deeds, lest you be put to shame in the Master's court. ॥59॥
1381.2: O Farid, serve the Master, and rid your heart of its doubt; dervishes need the endurance of trees. ॥60॥
1381.3: O Farid, black are my clothes, and black is my garb; I go about full of sins, and the world calls me a dervish. ॥61॥
1381.4: The scorched (crop) does not turn green again with water, even if one dips it in water; O Farid, she who is a forsaken soul-bride of God grieves and goes on grieving. ॥62॥
1381.5: When (a girl) is unmarried, there is eagerness (for marriage); once married, there are troubles; O Farid, (then) this is the regret: she cannot become unmarried again. ॥63॥
1381.6: Swans came and alighted on a little pond of salty ground; they dip their beaks but do not drink: they long to fly away. ॥64॥
The swan (hans, hanjh) stands for the pure in mind.
1381.7: A swan flew and alighted in a field of kodhra (coarse millet), and people go to drive it away; the heedless people do not know that the swan does not eat kodhra. ॥65॥
1381.8: The flocks of birds that made the pools lively have gone, one after another; O Farid, the full lake too will pass away, and the lotuses, left alone, have withered. ॥66॥
1381.9: O Farid, a brick for a pillow, sleep in the earth, and the worm biting into the flesh: many an age will pass, lying on one side. ॥67॥
1381.10: O Farid, the pitcher of lovely colour is broken, and the fine rope has snapped; in whose house is Azrail, the angel, a guest today? ॥68॥
Azrail (Azrael): in Islamic tradition, the angel of death, who takes the soul from the body.
1381.11: O Farid, the pitcher of lovely colour is broken, and the fine rope has snapped; how can those friends who were a burden on the earth come back today? ॥69॥
1381.12: O Farid, O dog who offers no namaz, this is not a good way to live; never once have you walked to the mosque at the five times (of prayer). ॥70॥
1381.13: Rise, O Farid, perform the wazu and offer the morning namaz; the head that does not bow to the Master: cut off that head and take it away. ॥71॥
Wazu (uju): the washing of the hands, face and feet before the namaz.
1381.14: The head that does not bow to the Master: what is to be done with that head? Let it be burnt under the pot in place of firewood. ॥72॥
1381.15: O Farid, where are your parents, who gave you birth? They have left you and gone, and still you are not convinced. ॥73॥
1381.16: O Farid, make your mind a level plain: take away its hollows and mounds; (then) hereafter the fire of hell will not come near you at all. ॥74॥
1381.17: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Farid, the Creator dwells within the creation, and the creation dwells in God; whom can we call bad, when there is no one without him? ॥75॥
1381.18: O Farid, (say, O midwife,) on the day my navel cord was cut, had you cut my throat a little too, such troubles would not have befallen me, nor would I bear such pains. ॥76॥
1381.19: The teeth, the legs, the eyes and the ears: they have all given way; the body wails aloud: those dear companions have gone. ॥77॥
1381.20: O Farid, do good to the one who does you ill; do not let anger dwell in your mind; (so) no disease touches the body, and everything comes into one's lap. ॥78॥
1382.1: O Farid, the flock of birds is a guest (here), and the world a lovely garden; the morning drum has sounded: make ready to go. ॥79॥
1382.2: O Farid, musk is shared out at night; those who sleep get no share; how shall those whose eyes are drowsy with sleep receive it? ॥80॥
1382.3: O Farid, I thought the pain was mine (alone), (but) the pain is in the whole world; when I climbed high and looked, this same fire was in every house. ॥81॥
1382.4: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Farid, the earth is delightful, (but) within it is a garden of poison; those whom the Pir (the Guru) has favoured are not touched by its heat. ॥82॥
1382.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Farid, lovely is life, and with it the body of fair colour; (but) rare are those to be found who love the Beloved. ॥83॥
1382.6: O stream, do not tear down the bank; you too will have to render an account; (but) the stream makes its way wherever God wills. ॥84॥
1382.7: O Farid, the day has gone in pains, and the night in anguish; the boatman stands and calls out: the boat is in the jaws of the whirlpool. ॥85॥
1382.8: The long, long river flows on, to bring down its banks; (but) what harm can the whirlpool do the boat, if the boatman stays watchful? ॥86॥
1382.9: O Farid, friends in word are twenty, (but) searching, I do not find one (true friend); I smoulder like dried dung for the sake of those beloved ones of mine. ॥87॥
1382.10: O Farid, this body keeps barking (with its wants); who would suffer it day after day? I will keep my ears stopped up, however hard the wind may blow. ॥88॥
1382.11: O Farid, God's dates are ripe, and rivers of honey are flowing; (but) with every day that goes by, hands are laid on (your) life. ॥89॥
1382.12: O Farid, the body has dried up and become a skeleton, and crows peck at the palms; (yet) even now that God has not come to (my) aid: see the fortune of man. ॥90॥
1382.13: The crows have rummaged through the skeleton and eaten up all the flesh; let none touch these two eyes: (in them is) the hope of seeing the Beloved. ॥91॥
1382.14: O crow, do not peck at my skeleton; fly off, if it is in your power; the skeleton in which my Husband dwells, do not eat the flesh from it. ॥92॥
1382.15: O Farid, the humble grave calls out: O homeless one, come home; to me you must surely come in the end; have no fear of dying. ॥93॥
1382.16: Before these eyes, so many have gone; O Farid, people have their own (cares), and I have mine. ॥94॥
1382.17: (If) you set yourself right, you will meet me, and meeting me, there is peace; O Farid, if you remain mine, the whole world will be yours. ॥95॥
1382.18: How long can the little tree on the river bank hold firm? O Farid, how long can water be kept in an unbaked pot? ॥96॥
1382.19: O Farid, the mansions are left empty, and the dwelling has come to be beneath the earth; those humble graves the souls will take as their own and sit in; O Sheikh, devote yourself to worship (bandagi): you must go, today or tomorrow. ॥97॥
1383.1: O Farid, the brink of death looks just like the river's crumbling bank; beyond, one hears, is blazing hell, (where) uproar and wailing arise; some have come to understand it all, (and) some go about without a care; the deeds done in the world are witnesses in the Lord's court. ॥98॥
1383.2: O Farid, a heron sits on the river bank at play; while this swan-like (heron) plays, hawks suddenly swoop on it; when God's hawks fall upon it, its play is forgotten; God has done such things as were never in (its) mind or thought. ॥99॥
1383.3: The body, three and a half maunds in weight, is kept going by water and grain; man came into the world, tying up his fond little hopes again and again; when the angel of death comes, breaking down all the doors, those dear brothers of his have bound him and handed him over; see, man has set off on the shoulders of four men. O Farid, the deeds done in the world: (those) were of use in the Lord's court. ॥100॥
1383.4: O Farid, I am a sacrifice to those birds whose dwelling is in the forest; they peck at pebbles and live on the bare ground, (yet) do not leave God's side. ॥101॥
1383.5: O Farid, the season has turned, the forest trembles, and the leaves keep falling; I have searched in the four directions: there is no staying anywhere. ॥102॥
1383.6: O Farid, let me tear my silken robe to rags, and wear a coarse blanket; let me put on those very garbs in which the Husband is met. ॥103॥
1383.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Why does she tear her silken robe, and put on a coarse blanket? O Nanak, even sitting at home the Husband is met, if she makes her intention right. ॥104॥
1383.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Farid, those who are proud of their greatness, of boundless wealth and youth, have gone away empty of the Master('s grace), like the mounds after the rain. ॥105॥
1383.9: O Farid, frightful are the faces of those who have forgotten the Name; here they suffer many pains, and hereafter they find no place or shelter. ॥106॥
1383.10: O Farid, you did not wake in the last part of the night: you are dead while still alive; if you have forgotten God, God has not forgotten you. ॥107॥
1383.11: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Farid, the Husband is full of delight, great and dependent on none; by being dyed in Allah, (one takes on) this true form. ॥108॥
1383.12: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Farid, take pain and pleasure as one, and remove the wrong from your heart; (take) what pleases Allah as good, and then you will find (his) court. ॥109॥
1383.13: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Farid, the world sounds as (Maya) plays it, and you too sound along with it; that soul alone does not sound so, whom Allah looks after. ॥110॥
1383.14: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Farid, the heart is dyed in this world, (yet) the world serves no purpose at all; the way of the fakirs is hard; it is gained by perfect grace. ॥111॥
1384.1: In the first watch (of the night, worship) is a little flower, and the fruit comes in the last part of the night; those who stay awake receive the gift from the Master. ॥112॥
1384.2: The gifts are the Master's; what force can prevail against him? Some, though awake, do not find (them), and others he wakes from their sleep and gives (them). ॥113॥
This salok is Guru Nanak Dev Ji's; it is also in Sri Raag ki Vaar (Ang 83).
1384.3: O you who search for your Husband, there is some flaw within you; those whose name is happy soul-bride look to no other. ॥114॥
1384.4: (If) patience within is the bow, (and) patience its bowstring, (and) patience the arrow, the Creator will not let it miss. ॥115॥
1384.5: The patient, in patience, burn away their bodies in this way; they are near to God (Khuda), and give their secret to no one. ॥116॥
1384.6: Patience is the very purpose (of life); if you, O man, make it firm (in yourself), you will grow into a river, and not shrink into a little stream. ॥117॥
1384.7: O Farid, the dervish's way is hard, and (your) love is only buttered on the surface; only a rare one has followed the way of the dervishes. ॥118॥
1384.8: (Let) the body burn like an oven, and the bones burn like firewood; (if) my feet tire, I will walk on my head, if (only) I may meet my Beloved. ॥119॥
1384.9: Do not heat the body as an oven is heated, nor burn the bones as firewood; what wrong have the head and the feet done (you)? Behold the Beloved within. ॥120॥
This salok is Guru Nanak Dev Ji's; it is also in Salok Varan te Vadhik (Ang 1411), with one word different.
1384.10: I go searching for my Friend, (yet) the Friend is with me; O Nanak, the Unseen cannot be seen; through the Guru, (he) shows (himself). ॥121॥
This salok, signed Nanak, is Guru Ram Das Ji's; it is also in Kanre ki Vaar (Ang 1318), with a few small differences of wording.
1384.11: Seeing the swans swimming, the herons grew eager; (but) the wretched herons drowned and died, heads down and feet up. ॥122॥
This salok and the next are Guru Amar Das Ji's; they are also in Vadhans ki Vaar (Ang 585), with a few small differences of wording.
1384.12: I took him for a great swan, and so I kept his company; had I known him to be a wretched heron, I would never have come near him at all. ॥123॥
1384.13: Be it swan or heron, what does it matter, when he casts his glance of grace on it? If it pleases him, O Nanak, he makes a swan out of a crow. ॥124॥
This salok, signed Nanak, is Guru Nanak Dev Ji's; it is also in Sri Raag ki Vaar (Ang 91), with a few small differences of wording.
1384.14: The bird of the lake is all alone, and the fowlers are fifty; this body is caught in the waves; O True One, (you are my only) hope. ॥125॥
1384.15: What is that word, what the virtue, and what that jewel of a mantra? What is that garb I should wear, by which the Husband comes under my sway? ॥126॥
1384.16: Humility is that word, forbearance the virtue, (a sweet) tongue the jewel of a mantra; put on these three garbs, O sister, and the Husband will come under your sway. ॥127॥
1384.17: One who, having wisdom, becomes as a child, having strength, becomes as the powerless, (and), having nothing, shares out what is his own: some such one may be called a devotee. ॥128॥
1384.18: Speak not (even) one harsh word: in all is the True Master; break no one's heart: all are priceless jewels. ॥129॥
1384.19: The minds of all are jewels; to break them is not good at all; if you long for the Beloved, break no one's heart. ॥130॥

1377.13: The saloks of Sheikh Farid Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The day on which the bride is to be wed, its appointed hour has been written beforehand;
the angel (of death), of whom one had only heard with one's ears, comes and shows his face;
the poor humble soul is drawn out (of the body), the bones made to crack.
The appointed hours that are written cannot be put off; make the soul understand this.
The soul is the bride, death the bridegroom: he will wed her and take her away.
Having sent (the soul) away with its own hands, on whose neck will (the body) run to fall?
Have you not heard with your ears of the Pul Sirat, finer than a hair?
O Farid, while the calls are sounding, do not stand by and let yourself be robbed. ॥1॥
1377.14: O Farid, the dervish's way at (the Lord's) door is hard, and I walk in the manner of the world;
I have tied up a bundle and lifted it: where shall I go and throw it down? ॥2॥
1378.1: Nothing is understood, nothing is seen: the world is a hidden fire.
My Master did well (by me); otherwise I too would have burned (in it). ॥3॥
1378.2: O Farid, had I known the sesame seeds were so few, I would have filled my cupped hands with care;
had I known my Husband was so young, I would have been less proud. ॥4॥
1378.3: Had I known the hem (I hold) would wear away, I would have tied a firm knot;
(O Master,) there is none as great as you for me: I have wandered and seen the whole world. ॥5॥
1378.4: O Farid, if you are of subtle understanding, do not write black records (of others);
bow your head and look within your own collar. ॥6॥
1378.5: O Farid, those who strike you with their fists, do not turn round and strike them;
having kissed their feet, let us go to our own home. ॥7॥
1378.6: O Farid, when it was your time to earn, you were steeped in the world;
the foundation of death grew firm, and when (the measure of life) was full, you had to depart. ॥8॥
1378.7: See, O Farid, what has come about: the beard has turned grey;
what lies ahead has come near, and what lies behind is left far away. ॥9॥
1378.8: See, O Farid, what has come about: sugar has turned to poison;
to whom but one's own Master can one tell this pain? ॥10॥
1378.9: O Farid, the eyes have grown weak with seeing, and the ears deaf with hearing;
the branch (of the body) has come to ripeness and is taking on another colour. ॥11॥
1378.10: O Farid, those who did not enjoy (the Husband) while their hair was black, hardly one of them enjoys him when it is grey;
love the Master, and the love will stay ever new. ॥12॥
1378.11: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Farid, in black hair or grey, the Master is ever (present), if one keeps him in mind;
(but) love does not take hold by one's own effort, though everyone may long for it;
this cup of love is the Master's: he gives it to whomever he pleases. ॥13॥
1378.12: O Farid, the eyes that enchanted the world, those eyes I have seen:
(once) they could not bear a line of kohl; they became a nest for the young of birds. ॥14॥
1378.13: O Farid, though one cries out and shouts and gives counsel day after day,
those whom Satan has led astray, how can they turn their minds (back)? ॥15॥
1378.14: O Farid, become (like) the grass on the path,
if you seek the Master in all;
(when) one tears you and others trample you,
then you will be admitted at the Master's door. ॥16॥
1378.15: O Farid, one should not speak ill of the dust; there is nothing as great as the dust:
while we live it is under our feet, and when we die it is over us. ॥17॥
1378.16: O Farid, where there is greed, what love can there be? With greed, love is false.
How long can the time be spent beneath a broken thatch when it rains? ॥18॥
1378.17: O Farid, why do you wander from forest to forest, trampling the thorns of the woods?
God dwells in the heart: why do you search the forest? ॥19॥
1378.18: O Farid, on these little legs I roamed deserts and mountains;
today, for me, Farid, the little water-pot (close by) has become a hundred kos away. ॥20॥
1378.19: O Farid, the nights are long, and the sides ache and smoulder;
cursed is the life of those who rest their hope on others. ॥21॥
1379.1: O Farid, if I ever hold back (anything) from friends who come to me,
my body burns like madder upon live coals. ॥22॥
1379.2: O Farid, the farmer wants the grapes of Bijaur, (yet) sows acacias;
he goes about having wool spun, and wants to wear silk. ॥23॥
1379.3: O Farid, the lane is muddy, the house is far, and I love the Beloved:
if I go, my blanket is soaked; if I stay, the love breaks. ॥24॥
1379.4: Let the blanket be soaked through and through, let the rain pour, as Allah wills;
I will go and meet those friends, and let the love not break. ॥25॥
1379.5: O Farid, I worry over my turban, lest it get soiled;
the heedless soul does not know that the dust eats up the head too. ॥26॥
1379.6: O Farid, brown sugar, white sugar, sugar candy, molasses, honey and buffalo's milk:
these things are all sweet, (yet), O God, they do not come up to you. ॥27॥
1379.7: O Farid, my bread is (dry) as wood, and my hunger is its relish;
those who have eaten buttered bread will suffer many pains. ॥28॥
1379.8: Eat your plain dry bread and drink cool water;
O Farid, seeing another's buttered bread, let no one make his heart yearn. ॥29॥
1379.9: Today I did not sleep with my Husband, and my body aches as if it would break;
go and ask the forsaken soul-brides: how does your night pass? ॥30॥
1379.10: She finds no shelter in her in-laws' home, and no place in her parents' home;
her Husband does not ask after her at all, (yet) the bride's name is happy soul-bride. ॥31॥
1379.11: In her in-laws' home and in her parents' home (alike, the bride) belongs to the Husband; the Husband is beyond reach and fathomless;
O Nanak, she is the happy soul-bride who pleases the carefree Lord. ॥32॥
1379.12: Bathed, washed and adorned, she came and slept without a care;
O Farid, she remained smeared with (the smell of) asafoetida, and the scent of musk was gone. ॥33॥
1379.13: I do not fear the going of youth, if the love of the Husband does not go;
O Farid, many a youth, without (his) love, has withered and dried up. ॥34॥
1379.14: O Farid, anxiety is my little bed, pain is its weave, and in separation (the same pain) is my mattress and quilt;
this is our life: see it, O True Master. ॥35॥
1379.15: Separation, separation, one cries; (yet) O pang of separation, you are the king.
O Farid, the body in which the pang of separation does not arise, know that body to be a cremation ground. ॥36॥
1379.16: O Farid, these (things of the world) are shoots of poison, coated in sugar and set out;
some died while still sowing them, and some went, leaving what they had sown to ruin. ॥37॥
1379.17: O Farid, four (watches of the day) you wasted roaming about, and four (of the night) you wasted in sleep;
God will ask for the account: for what work did you come? ॥38॥
1379.18: O Farid, have you gone to a door, to a gateway, and seen the gong (gharial)?
Blameless, it is beaten: what will become of us, who are to blame? ॥39॥
1379.19: Hour after hour it is beaten, and at every watch it receives its punishment;
like the gong is that body whose night passes in pain. ॥40॥
1380.1: Sheikh Farid has grown old; his body has started to shake;
even were one to live a hundred years, the body will still become dust. ॥41॥
1380.2: O Farid, (say,) O Master, do not let me sit at the door of another;
if you would keep me so, draw the life out of my body. ॥42॥
1380.3: With an axe on his shoulder and a pitcher on his head, the blacksmith is master over the forest;
O Farid, I seek my Husband, and you seek charcoal. ॥43॥
1380.4: O Farid, some have flour in plenty, and some have not even salt;
when they have gone on ahead, they will be known (for what they are): (there it will be seen) who is to be beaten. ॥44॥
1380.5: (Those who had) kettle-drums beside them, a canopy over their heads, trumpets and songs of praise,
have gone to sleep in the graveyard, and become one with the orphans. ॥45॥
1380.6: O Farid, those who built houses, pavilions and mansions have gone too;
they made a false bargain, and came and lay down in graves. ॥46॥
1380.7: O Farid, the patched coat has many stitches, (but) the soul has not a single stitch;
each in his turn, the great sheikhs and the sheikhs have gone. ॥47॥
1380.8: O Farid, while the two lamps (of the eyes) were burning, the angel (of death) came and sat down;
he seized the fort (of the body), plundered the heart, and went, putting out the little lamps. ॥48॥
1380.9: O Farid, see what has befallen the cotton, what has befallen the sesame,
the sugar-cane and the paper, the clay pot and the charcoal:
such is the punishment of those who do evil deeds. ॥49॥
1380.10: O Farid, the prayer mat on the shoulder, the black woollen robe about the neck, a knife in the heart and molasses in the mouth:
outside there seems to be light, and in the heart is the dark night. ॥50॥
1380.11: O Farid, not a drop of blood comes out, if one cuts open (their) body;
the bodies that are dyed in God, in those bodies there is no blood. ॥51॥
1380.12: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
This body is all blood; without blood there is no body.
Those who are dyed in their Husband: in that body is no blood of greed.
When the fear (of God) enters, the body grows lean, and the blood of greed goes out of it.
As metal is purified in fire, so the fear of the Lord removes the filth of an evil mind.
O Nanak, beautiful are those people who, giving their love to the Lord, are dyed (in him). ॥52॥
1380.13: O Farid, search out that pool from which the real thing is found;
what comes of searching a puddle? The hand only sinks in the mud. ॥53॥
1380.14: O Farid, when young, she did not enjoy her Husband, and grown old, she died;
in the grave the bride cries out that she did not meet you, O Husband. ॥54॥
1380.15: O Farid, the head has turned white, the beard is white, and the moustache too is white;
O heedless, crazy mind, why do you indulge in pleasures? ॥55॥
1380.16: O Farid, how far can one run on a rooftop? Cast off this sleep that keeps you from the Beloved;
the numbered days you were given have gone, leaping away. ॥56॥
1380.17: O Farid, houses, pavilions and mansions: let no one fix his mind on these;
when the unweighed earth falls (on you in the grave), none (of them) will be your friend. ॥57॥
1380.18: O Farid, do not set your heart on pavilions and wealth; keep mighty death in mind;
remember that place to which you must go in the end. ॥58॥
1381.1: O Farid, the deeds that bring no good, give up those wretched deeds,
lest you be put to shame in the Master's court. ॥59॥
1381.2: O Farid, serve the Master, and rid your heart of its doubt;
dervishes need the endurance of trees. ॥60॥
1381.3: O Farid, black are my clothes, and black is my garb;
I go about full of sins, and the world calls me a dervish. ॥61॥
1381.4: The scorched (crop) does not turn green again with water, even if one dips it in water;
O Farid, she who is a forsaken soul-bride of God grieves and goes on grieving. ॥62॥
1381.5: When (a girl) is unmarried, there is eagerness (for marriage); once married, there are troubles;
O Farid, (then) this is the regret: she cannot become unmarried again. ॥63॥
1381.6: Swans came and alighted on a little pond of salty ground;
they dip their beaks but do not drink: they long to fly away. ॥64॥
1381.7: A swan flew and alighted in a field of kodhra (coarse millet), and people go to drive it away;
the heedless people do not know that the swan does not eat kodhra. ॥65॥
1381.8: The flocks of birds that made the pools lively have gone, one after another;
O Farid, the full lake too will pass away, and the lotuses, left alone, have withered. ॥66॥
1381.9: O Farid, a brick for a pillow, sleep in the earth, and the worm biting into the flesh:
many an age will pass, lying on one side. ॥67॥
1381.10: O Farid, the pitcher of lovely colour is broken, and the fine rope has snapped;
in whose house is Azrail, the angel, a guest today? ॥68॥
1381.11: O Farid, the pitcher of lovely colour is broken, and the fine rope has snapped;
how can those friends who were a burden on the earth come back today? ॥69॥
1381.12: O Farid, O dog who offers no namaz, this is not a good way to live;
never once have you walked to the mosque at the five times (of prayer). ॥70॥
1381.13: Rise, O Farid, perform the wazu and offer the morning namaz;
the head that does not bow to the Master: cut off that head and take it away. ॥71॥
1381.14: The head that does not bow to the Master: what is to be done with that head?
Let it be burnt under the pot in place of firewood. ॥72॥
1381.15: O Farid, where are your parents, who gave you birth?
They have left you and gone, and still you are not convinced. ॥73॥
1381.16: O Farid, make your mind a level plain: take away its hollows and mounds;
(then) hereafter the fire of hell will not come near you at all. ॥74॥
1381.17: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Farid, the Creator dwells within the creation, and the creation dwells in God;
whom can we call bad, when there is no one without him? ॥75॥
1381.18: O Farid, (say, O midwife,) on the day my navel cord was cut, had you cut my throat a little too,
such troubles would not have befallen me, nor would I bear such pains. ॥76॥
1381.19: The teeth, the legs, the eyes and the ears: they have all given way;
the body wails aloud: those dear companions have gone. ॥77॥
1381.20: O Farid, do good to the one who does you ill; do not let anger dwell in your mind;
(so) no disease touches the body, and everything comes into one's lap. ॥78॥
1382.1: O Farid, the flock of birds is a guest (here), and the world a lovely garden;
the morning drum has sounded: make ready to go. ॥79॥
1382.2: O Farid, musk is shared out at night; those who sleep get no share;
how shall those whose eyes are drowsy with sleep receive it? ॥80॥
1382.3: O Farid, I thought the pain was mine (alone), (but) the pain is in the whole world;
when I climbed high and looked, this same fire was in every house. ॥81॥
1382.4: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Farid, the earth is delightful, (but) within it is a garden of poison;
those whom the Pir (the Guru) has favoured are not touched by its heat. ॥82॥
1382.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Farid, lovely is life, and with it the body of fair colour;
(but) rare are those to be found who love the Beloved. ॥83॥
1382.6: O stream, do not tear down the bank; you too will have to render an account;
(but) the stream makes its way wherever God wills. ॥84॥
1382.7: O Farid, the day has gone in pains, and the night in anguish;
the boatman stands and calls out: the boat is in the jaws of the whirlpool. ॥85॥
1382.8: The long, long river flows on, to bring down its banks;
(but) what harm can the whirlpool do the boat, if the boatman stays watchful? ॥86॥
1382.9: O Farid, friends in word are twenty, (but) searching, I do not find one (true friend);
I smoulder like dried dung for the sake of those beloved ones of mine. ॥87॥
1382.10: O Farid, this body keeps barking (with its wants); who would suffer it day after day?
I will keep my ears stopped up, however hard the wind may blow. ॥88॥
1382.11: O Farid, God's dates are ripe, and rivers of honey are flowing;
(but) with every day that goes by, hands are laid on (your) life. ॥89॥
1382.12: O Farid, the body has dried up and become a skeleton, and crows peck at the palms;
(yet) even now that God has not come to (my) aid: see the fortune of man. ॥90॥
1382.13: The crows have rummaged through the skeleton and eaten up all the flesh;
let none touch these two eyes: (in them is) the hope of seeing the Beloved. ॥91॥
1382.14: O crow, do not peck at my skeleton; fly off, if it is in your power;
the skeleton in which my Husband dwells, do not eat the flesh from it. ॥92॥
1382.15: O Farid, the humble grave calls out: O homeless one, come home;
to me you must surely come in the end; have no fear of dying. ॥93॥
1382.16: Before these eyes, so many have gone;
O Farid, people have their own (cares), and I have mine. ॥94॥
1382.17: (If) you set yourself right, you will meet me, and meeting me, there is peace;
O Farid, if you remain mine, the whole world will be yours. ॥95॥
1382.18: How long can the little tree on the river bank hold firm?
O Farid, how long can water be kept in an unbaked pot? ॥96॥
1382.19: O Farid, the mansions are left empty, and the dwelling has come to be beneath the earth;
those humble graves the souls will take as their own and sit in;
O Sheikh, devote yourself to worship (bandagi): you must go, today or tomorrow. ॥97॥
1383.1: O Farid, the brink of death looks just like the river's crumbling bank;
beyond, one hears, is blazing hell, (where) uproar and wailing arise;
some have come to understand it all, (and) some go about without a care;
the deeds done in the world are witnesses in the Lord's court. ॥98॥
1383.2: O Farid, a heron sits on the river bank at play;
while this swan-like (heron) plays, hawks suddenly swoop on it;
when God's hawks fall upon it, its play is forgotten;
God has done such things as were never in (its) mind or thought. ॥99॥
1383.3: The body, three and a half maunds in weight, is kept going by water and grain;
man came into the world, tying up his fond little hopes again and again;
when the angel of death comes, breaking down all the doors,
those dear brothers of his have bound him and handed him over;
see, man has set off on the shoulders of four men.
O Farid, the deeds done in the world: (those) were of use in the Lord's court. ॥100॥
1383.4: O Farid, I am a sacrifice to those birds whose dwelling is in the forest;
they peck at pebbles and live on the bare ground, (yet) do not leave God's side. ॥101॥
1383.5: O Farid, the season has turned, the forest trembles, and the leaves keep falling;
I have searched in the four directions: there is no staying anywhere. ॥102॥
1383.6: O Farid, let me tear my silken robe to rags, and wear a coarse blanket;
let me put on those very garbs in which the Husband is met. ॥103॥
1383.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Why does she tear her silken robe, and put on a coarse blanket?
O Nanak, even sitting at home the Husband is met, if she makes her intention right. ॥104॥
1383.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Farid, those who are proud of their greatness, of boundless wealth and youth,
have gone away empty of the Master('s grace), like the mounds after the rain. ॥105॥
1383.9: O Farid, frightful are the faces of those who have forgotten the Name;
here they suffer many pains, and hereafter they find no place or shelter. ॥106॥
1383.10: O Farid, you did not wake in the last part of the night: you are dead while still alive;
if you have forgotten God, God has not forgotten you. ॥107॥
1383.11: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Farid, the Husband is full of delight, great and dependent on none;
by being dyed in Allah, (one takes on) this true form. ॥108॥
1383.12: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Farid, take pain and pleasure as one, and remove the wrong from your heart;
(take) what pleases Allah as good, and then you will find (his) court. ॥109॥
1383.13: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Farid, the world sounds as (Maya) plays it, and you too sound along with it;
that soul alone does not sound so, whom Allah looks after. ॥110॥
1383.14: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Farid, the heart is dyed in this world, (yet) the world serves no purpose at all;
the way of the fakirs is hard; it is gained by perfect grace. ॥111॥
1384.1: In the first watch (of the night, worship) is a little flower, and the fruit comes in the last part of the night;
those who stay awake receive the gift from the Master. ॥112॥
1384.2: The gifts are the Master's; what force can prevail against him?
Some, though awake, do not find (them), and others he wakes from their sleep and gives (them). ॥113॥
1384.3: O you who search for your Husband, there is some flaw within you;
those whose name is happy soul-bride look to no other. ॥114॥
1384.4: (If) patience within is the bow, (and) patience its bowstring,
(and) patience the arrow, the Creator will not let it miss. ॥115॥
1384.5: The patient, in patience, burn away their bodies in this way;
they are near to God (Khuda), and give their secret to no one. ॥116॥
1384.6: Patience is the very purpose (of life); if you, O man, make it firm (in yourself),
you will grow into a river, and not shrink into a little stream. ॥117॥
1384.7: O Farid, the dervish's way is hard, and (your) love is only buttered on the surface;
only a rare one has followed the way of the dervishes. ॥118॥
1384.8: (Let) the body burn like an oven, and the bones burn like firewood;
(if) my feet tire, I will walk on my head, if (only) I may meet my Beloved. ॥119॥
1384.9: Do not heat the body as an oven is heated, nor burn the bones as firewood;
what wrong have the head and the feet done (you)? Behold the Beloved within. ॥120॥
1384.10: I go searching for my Friend, (yet) the Friend is with me;
O Nanak, the Unseen cannot be seen; through the Guru, (he) shows (himself). ॥121॥
1384.11: Seeing the swans swimming, the herons grew eager;
(but) the wretched herons drowned and died, heads down and feet up. ॥122॥
1384.12: I took him for a great swan, and so I kept his company;
had I known him to be a wretched heron, I would never have come near him at all. ॥123॥
1384.13: Be it swan or heron, what does it matter, when he casts his glance of grace on it?
If it pleases him, O Nanak, he makes a swan out of a crow. ॥124॥
1384.14: The bird of the lake is all alone, and the fowlers are fifty;
this body is caught in the waves; O True One, (you are my only) hope. ॥125॥
1384.15: What is that word, what the virtue, and what that jewel of a mantra?
What is that garb I should wear, by which the Husband comes under my sway? ॥126॥
1384.16: Humility is that word, forbearance the virtue, (a sweet) tongue the jewel of a mantra;
put on these three garbs, O sister, and the Husband will come under your sway. ॥127॥
1384.17: One who, having wisdom, becomes as a child,
having strength, becomes as the powerless,
(and), having nothing, shares out what is his own:
some such one may be called a devotee. ॥128॥
1384.18: Speak not (even) one harsh word: in all is the True Master;
break no one's heart: all are priceless jewels. ॥129॥
1384.19: The minds of all are jewels; to break them is not good at all;
if you long for the Beloved, break no one's heart. ॥130॥
